subject.title: All .large bubbles should have scrollable body regardless of truncation

question: Should native chat use an independently scrollable bounded body for every large/tall bubble, or retain transcript-only scrolling except for a narrower long-content reader affordance?
rationale: Current code does not define a shared large-bubble contract, and nested scrolling changes mobile gesture, accessibility, and streaming behavior across two native implementations.

options.title: Define always-scrollable large bodies
options.body: Adopt the requested interaction model and specify the shared size bound, nested-scroll behavior, accessibility semantics, and iOS/Android parity requirements.

options.title: Specify a narrower reader policy
options.body: Keep transcript-first scrolling and add an explicit bounded reader only for objectively oversized or truncated content, with clear activation criteria.

options.title: Decline nested scrolling
options.body: Retain the existing transcript-level interaction model and close the request only after documenting why a per-bubble reader is not desired.

recommendation.title: Specify a narrower reader policy
recommendation.body: Keep transcript-first scrolling and add an explicit bounded reader only for objectively oversized or truncated content, with clear activation criteria.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent issue review and release-area history make Peter Steinberger the strongest available routing candidate for the native-chat interaction decision.
